topic:
ANCHOR_PHRASE: Support-active completeness for fixed-support systematic-selection data fusion.

ACADEMIC_FIELD: Graphical causal identification under systematic selection

MODE: gap

CLUSTER: scm

AXIS: (a)/(i)

MOTIF: M19

TARGET_TIER: field

FIELD_CONTRACT: Prove an expansion-aware support normalization and an all-branch formula-or-global-twin completeness theorem. A line-9-only patch, the terminal three-observable classification alone, or generic response-function quantifier elimination is below field.

BACKGROUND: Lee-Ghassami-Shpitser 2024 Algorithms 1-2 and Theorems 4-5 give a sound systematic-selection recursion, branchwise nonidentification results, and an explicit completeness conjecture. Tabell-Tikka-Karvanen 2026 adds general data-fusion pruning and clustering but no fixed-support selector converse. Direct primary and follow-up searches found no completion.

MODEL_REGIME: Input is a finite selector-gated semi-Markovian LS-DAG expansion G+ with explicit latent roots, selector-controlled structural equations, fixed finite alphabets, observed nodes V and random selector S, and a declared fixed selector support H. Observe the complete joint law p(V,S) on H, with epsilon-positive structurally admissible cells. Target p(Y(a,S=empty)), where do(S=empty) sets every selector intervention indicator to zero. Models share G+ and H and vary over its finite canonical response-function tables and latent-root laws.

LIVE_OPPORTUNITY: Fixed selector support changes both positive identification and nonidentification witnesses. The missing result is support normalization plus a converse that never adds an unsupplied context.

GROUNDING: Published SS-ID interleaves selection correction, district factorization, and fixing. The first changed proof step is to substitute support-constant selector gates while retaining the exact parameter image, then derive a residual rational-rule-or-common-contrast alternative whose twin compiler preserves all contexts simultaneously.

KERNEL: Define N_H(G+) as the explicit normalized response-function expansion: substitute selector components constant on H and at the target, delete only unused arguments, retain every latent root/response parameter, and mark natural-mechanism holes invoked only by the target. Prove mutual inverse parameter maps between G+ and N_H(G+) and equality of their attainable observed-target relation. Construct a terminating SA-CS-ID calculus on the normalized expansion and retained image constraints that returns exactly either (I) a rational circuit in p(V,S)|H valid for every compatible model or (II) two canonical response-table models plus an open rational parameter box, with support exactly H, identical admissible observed cells, and different targets. Prove soundness, completeness over every residual branch, preservation of valid published positive derivations, and termination by a decreasing finite state measure. A marked support-hole ancestor may terminate in II but must supply the legal pair. Projection may organize elimination but may not enlarge the model class.

FOCAL_OBJECT: The normalized explicit expansion N_H(G+), its retained parameter-image constraints, and SA-CS-ID formula-or-global-twin certificate.

COMPUTATION: Substitute fixed gates in explicit response tables; use labelled projection only to organize fixing and induced-width variable elimination; carry image constraints through recursion; verify twin tables algebraically. Exhaustively compare binary expansions through four observed nodes/two selector components with exact response-function equations at fixed H.

ESTIMATION_RUNG: Evaluate returned rational circuits with empirical p(V,S)|H; on an epsilon-positive differentiable interior derive the finite-table influence function and pointwise Wald inference. Boundary-uniform inference is delegated and not the headline.

CONSUMER: The CRAN dosearch package (Tikka-Hyttinen-Karvanen, JSS 2021, current 1.0.12) identifies effects from multiple sources and supports selection bias and context-specific independence. An optional provenance-aware CS-SCM backend would return a valid formula or exact twin/missing-context certificate without silently adding contexts.

MINIMAL_INSTANCE: Two exact binary fixed-H models in the presolve draft. With S->A,S->Y,A->Y,A<->Y,S<->Y, d=(-4,-1,0,3) preserves all six observed cells (minimum 11/96) but moves the target 1/2 to 63/128. Removing A<->Y yields an adjustment-identified neighbor with value 7/12 after inactive-gate normalization. The calculus must classify them differently without changing H.

PRIOR_ART: Lee-Ghassami-Shpitser 2024 https://arxiv.org/abs/2404.06602; Tabell-Tikka-Karvanen 2026 https://www.jmlr.org/papers/v27/25-1140.html; dosearch https://www.jstatsoft.org/article/view/v099i05. The candidate adds fixed-support parameter-image normalization and global all-branch twins. Queue/claims/bank checks found no collision.

EST_ACHIEVABLE_TIER: field

CEILING_REASON: Full support-aware constructive completeness resolves a new identification regime and changes a live software workflow; finite graph-specific scope keeps it below flagship.

LIKELY_DEATH: General residuals may require nonrational semialgebraic functionals, or common contrasts may fail to lift through interacting districts while preserving H.

PRESOLVE EVIDENCE REQUIRING VERIFICATION: Retained-parameter normalization was derived, and a complete terminal three-observable classification was proved: usable-context coverage gives identification, while a tensor-product response contrast gives every negative case. Exact arithmetic verified 78 formula cases and 78 twin cases, plus the 7/12 formula and 1/2 versus 63/128 twins. Checks covered inactive gates, natural-mechanism holes, all treatment/selection-confounding patterns, positivity, rationality risks, generic-elimination collapse, and consumer fit.
UNRESOLVED BOTTLENECK: Prove that every irreducible normalized residual admits an observable rational reduction or a common response contrast that lifts through interacting districts and fixed kernels while preserving the complete observed law and exactly H.
EARLY KILL TEST: Replay the paired examples and 156 terminal configurations through the recursion, add one observed mediator at the same two contexts, and compare every certificate with exact response-table equations; any changed observed cell/H or an identified nonrational residual forces pivot.
STRONGEST-FORM DRAFT (unverified, gaps listed inside): <repo-root>/internal/presolve_drafts/scm_fixedsupport_complete_id.md.

open_problems.open_problem: Is there a sound and complete identification calculus for p(Y(a,S=empty)) from the fixed-support law p(V,S)|H that returns either a support-valid formula or two models agreeing on every supplied cell and differing on the target?

source_refs.claim: The systematic-selection algorithm is sound, proves nonidentification for all but one failure case, and is explicitly conjectured complete.
source_refs.author: Jaron J. R. Lee, AmirEmad Ghassami, Ilya Shpitser

source_refs.claim: General-identification completeness depends on the exact positivity regime; correcting positivity invalidates an earlier proof and requires a new reduction.
source_refs.author: Yaroslav Kivva, Ehsan Mokhtarian, Jalal Etesami, Negar Kiyavash

source_refs.excerpt: Construct equal observed behavior laws with finite hidden refinements having opposite overlap status.

open_problems.why_unsolved: Lee et al. leave an explicit completeness conjecture after proving soundness and constructing witnesses for most failed branches. Classical hedge and thicket arguments can treat supplied contexts as separately indexed distributions, but fixed H simultaneously excludes unsupplied contexts and imposes cross-context equalities through shared selector-gated mechanisms. Kivva et al. show that even ordinary gID completeness is sensitive to the precise positivity regime. The prior proposal independently isolates the analogous obstruction in a latent-state setting: local hidden refinements must be coupled so that all observed regimes remain equal simultaneously. Here the first unresolved proof step is to lift a residual response-table contrast through interacting districts and fixed kernels while remaining inside the retained parameter image, preserving every cell in H, and creating no new context.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A terminating completeness theorem partitioning every finite fixed-H CS-SCM instance into either a rational circuit in p(V,S)|H or two finite canonical response-table models on an open rational parameter box with support exactly H, identical complete observed laws on H, and unequal target values.

writing_exemplar.why: It supplies the exact selector-model vocabulary, recursive algorithm, partial converse, and explicit completeness conjecture.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: heterogeneous datasets arise through systematic selection -> selector mechanisms impose context-specific restrictions beyond gID -> SS-ID exploits those restrictions but leaves one failure class unresolved -> fixed-support formula-or-global-twin completeness closes that class

method_exemplars.technique: Reduce a positivity-qualified general-identification problem to classical ID subproblems and transport complete failure witnesses through the reduction.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The required calculus likewise needs a support-correct reduction whose negative certificates remain valid under the exact available-data regime.

method_exemplars.technique: Reduce identification with control-variable context-specific independences to finitely many ordinary graph-identification instances and prove completeness by functional approximation.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Selector components are control-like context variables, but the destination must preserve endogenous selector sharing and a restricted context support.

method_exemplars.technique: Translate fixing-derived identifying functionals into influence-function and weight-based estimators with asymptotic theory.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Every positive branch produces a finite observed-law functional whose inference should be derived from the returned circuit.

open_problems.open_problem: Can fixed selector support be compiled into an explicit response-function normal form by substituting support-constant gates while preserving exactly the attainable observed-target relation?

source_refs.claim: CS-SCMs encode mechanism invariance through selector-gated structural equations and exploit the resulting context-specific restrictions.
source_refs.author: Jaron J. R. Lee, AmirEmad Ghassami, Ilya Shpitser

source_refs.claim: Logical and parameter constraints can alter causal identifiability, and arithmetic circuits can test query invariance under such constraints.
source_refs.author: Yizuo Chen, Adnan Darwiche

source_refs.claim: Every discrete-SCM counterfactual law has a finite canonical-SCM representation suitable for polynomial optimization.
source_refs.author: Junzhe Zhang, Jin Tian, Elias Bareinboim

open_problems.why_unsolved: This is a technique-derived direction rather than a gap asserted verbatim by the cited papers. Lee et al. reason through context-selected latent projections but do not construct a fixed-H canonical expansion with inverse parameter maps. Chen and Darwiche compile constraints for invariance testing without separating selector arguments made constant by H from natural-mechanism entries used only by the target. Zhang et al. provide finite response tables without preserving the shared selector-gate parameter image. The first missing proof step is therefore an exact substitution lemma that deletes only genuinely unused arguments, retains every latent-root and response parameter needed by either the observations or target, and maps both ways without introducing an unsupplied context.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: An explicit normalization N_H(G+) with mutually inverse parameter maps between the original and normalized finite response-table models and a proof that their attainable sets of pairs (p(V,S)|H, p(Y(a,S=empty))) are equal.

writing_exemplar.why: Its framing explains why parameter-level constraints can change graphical identifiability and therefore belong in the formal problem input.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: a graph alone describes too large a model class -> logical and equality constraints shrink its parameter image -> constrained identifiability can differ from ordinary do-calculus -> selector-support constraints require an exact normal form before identification

method_exemplars.technique: Replace arbitrary latent variables by finite canonical response types and express observable and counterfactual probabilities as polynomials in their masses.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The desired normalization is an equality between finite response-function parameter images, with the additional obligation to preserve selector-gate sharing.

method_exemplars.technique: Compile causal models and parameter constraints into arithmetic circuits and test whether the target circuit is invariant over observationally equivalent parameters.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Circuit invariance is structurally analogous to equality of the original and normalized observed-target relations, although the required result must add constructive inverse maps.

open_problems.open_problem: Can pruning and clustering for causal data fusion be strengthened to an if-and-only-if reduction on fixed-support systematic-selection models, with both identifying formulas and support-exact nonidentification twins liftable through the reduction?

source_refs.claim: The paper supplies sufficient pruning and clustering conditions and transfers identifiability or nonidentifiability from reduced multi-source graphs.
source_refs.author: Otto Tabell, Santtu Tikka, Juha Karvanen

source_refs.claim: Graph pruning can preserve identification and simplify identifying functionals for a single data source under stated sufficient conditions.
source_refs.author: Santtu Tikka, Juha Karvanen

source_refs.claim: Systematic-selection identification interleaves selector correction, district factorization, reachability, and fixing.
source_refs.author: Jaron J. R. Lee, AmirEmad Ghassami, Ilya Shpitser

open_problems.why_unsolved: Tabell et al. prove sufficient graphical reductions for collections of supplied observational or experimental inputs, not exact parameter-image equivalence for an endogenous selector with declared support. Under fixed H, deleting or clustering a node can erase a support-constant gate equality or a target-only natural-mechanism hole even when ordinary ancestry permits removal. The first proof step that changes is the reduction lemma itself: it must act on the normalized response-table image and provide inverse lifts instead of only comparing reduced and original graphs.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: Necessary and sufficient pruning and clustering conditions for N_H(G+), together with constructive maps lifting every reduced identifying circuit and every reduced support-exact twin pair to the original expansion without changing H.

writing_exemplar.why: It motivates graph reduction through the computational cost of general data-fusion identification and states preservation questions in the closest destination language.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: general data-fusion reasoning grows rapidly with graph size -> pruning and clustering can preserve essential identification structure -> published conditions are sufficient for ordinary multi-source inputs -> fixed-support selectors require exact image-preserving reductions

method_exemplars.technique: Relate causal models, available source distributions, and identifying functionals before and after graph pruning or clustering.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The destination is the same reduction problem with support-specific gate constraints added to every object that must be preserved.

method_exemplars.technique: Use finite canonical response types to construct explicit model transformations and compare attainable counterfactual distributions.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Response-type maps can make formula and twin lifts explicit rather than relying only on graphical sufficiency.

method_exemplars.technique: Derive estimators and influence functions directly from fixing-based causal functionals in hidden-variable graphs.
method_exemplars.why_closest: A successful reduction should preserve the estimable functional and its first-order behavior, not merely point identification.

open_problems.open_problem: When a fixed-support systematic-selection target is not point identified, what are its sharp graph-native bounds after enforcing all selector-gate equalities and excluding every context outside H?

source_refs.claim: The systematic-selection paper identifies informative bounds as a natural response to nonidentification but develops point identification instead.
source_refs.author: Jaron J. R. Lee, AmirEmad Ghassami, Ilya Shpitser

source_refs.claim: Canonical finite SCMs turn sharp counterfactual bounds from heterogeneous observational and experimental data into polynomial programs.
source_refs.author: Junzhe Zhang, Jin Tian, Elias Bareinboim

source_refs.claim: Recent data-fusion partial identification derives bounds and doubly robust endpoint estimators under failures of confounding and study-exchangeability assumptions.
source_refs.author: Quinn Lanners, Cynthia Rudin, Alexander Volfovsky, Harsh Parikh

open_problems.why_unsolved: The canonical-SCM polynomial program accepts collections of supplied observational or experimental laws, whereas a random selector observed jointly with V creates cross-context restrictions through one gated mechanism and requires the feasible set to have support exactly H. Dropping the shared-mechanism image constraints can widen the bound, while introducing distributions for absent selector values can narrow it illicitly. Existing sensitivity-based fusion bounds use different potential-outcome restrictions and do not enforce the graph-native selector image.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A finite polynomial or equivalent semialgebraic characterization whose extrema are the sharp lower and upper bounds of p(Y(a,S=empty)) over exactly the response-table models inducing p(V,S)|H with support H, including a theorem characterizing when the interval collapses to a point.

writing_exemplar.why: It frames partial counterfactual identification from heterogeneous data as optimization over all causally compatible models.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: heterogeneous laws need not point-identify a counterfactual -> discrete SCMs admit finite canonical response types -> compatible models define an optimization problem -> selector-support image constraints should yield sharp fixed-H bounds

method_exemplars.technique: Enumerate canonical response functions and optimize a counterfactual polynomial subject to exact observed and interventional probability equations.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The desired bounds have the same optimization structure after selector-gate sharing and exact-H constraints are imposed.

method_exemplars.technique: Construct orthogonal scores and double-machine-learning estimators for data-fusion bound endpoints, with endpoint limit theory.
method_exemplars.why_closest: If fixed-H sharp endpoints are smooth value functionals on a stable active set, analogous debiasing machinery can support inference.

open_problems.open_problem: Can one characterize the inclusion-minimal selector contexts that must be added to fixed support H to identify a target that currently admits a support-preserving twin witness?

source_refs.claim: When do-search cannot identify an effect, its search can help determine additional data sources or assumptions that would make identification possible.
source_refs.author: Santtu Tikka, Antti Hyttinen, Juha Karvanen

source_refs.claim: In CS-SCMs, selector values represent observational or experimental contexts generated by an explicit and potentially confounded selection process.
source_refs.author: Jaron J. R. Lee, AmirEmad Ghassami, Ilya Shpitser

source_refs.claim: gID supplies a sound and complete criterion for identification from an arbitrary collection of observational and experimental distributions.
source_refs.author: Sanghack Lee, Juan D. Correa, Elias Bareinboim

open_problems.why_unsolved: do-search can seek additional source distributions and gID treats arbitrary experiment collections, but both regard sources as separately supplied laws. In a systematic-selection model, adding a selector context is not a free syntactic input: it must remain compatible with the same selector mechanism, may activate previously constant gates, and changes the exact support requirement. The first changed proof step is to convert a fixed-H twin contrast into constraints identifying which added contexts separate the twins, and then prove that the chosen contexts eliminate all witnesses rather than only one local pair.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A finite characterization or terminating algorithm returning all inclusion-minimal supersets H' of H for which the target has an identifying functional, together with a formula for each successful H' and a surviving support-exact twin for every insufficient augmentation.

writing_exemplar.why: It motivates identification software as a study-design tool capable of indicating what additional evidence would resolve a failed query.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: causal evidence is distributed across incomplete sources -> automated search determines whether current sources identify the target -> failure can guide additional data collection -> fixed-support selector models require minimal context additions that remain structurally legal

method_exemplars.technique: Use hedgelets and thickets to characterize which collections of interventional distributions identify a causal query.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Minimal selector-context augmentation can be formulated as eliminating every surviving thicket-like witness subject to shared-mechanism constraints.

method_exemplars.technique: Search over do-calculus with arbitrary input distributions and use failed search states to identify useful additional sources.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The desired result is a provenance-aware version of the same evidence-design search over legal selector contexts.

open_problems.open_problem: Can the influence function and pointwise Wald limit law for every differentiable rational circuit returned by a fixed-support systematic-selection identifier be generated mechanically from the joint finite-table law on H?

source_refs.claim: The paper derives influence-function and weight-based estimators for broad hidden-variable graphical classes whose identifying functionals can be difficult to use directly.
source_refs.author: Rohit Bhattacharya, Razieh Nabi, Ilya Shpitser

source_refs.claim: The paper characterizes efficiency gains and constructs efficient estimators when different data sources align with components of a target distribution.
source_refs.author: Sijia Li, Alex Luedtke

source_refs.claim: Universal influence-function results are developed for sources aligned with conditional distributions that need not share one ordinary factorization.
source_refs.author: Ellen Graham, Marco Carone, Andrea Rotnitzky

source_refs.claim: The explicit selector induces one coherent joint data-generating distribution, while the paper concentrates on identification rather than estimation.
source_refs.author: Jaron J. R. Lee, AmirEmad Ghassami, Ilya Shpitser

open_problems.why_unsolved: Bhattacharya et al. derive estimators for ordinary hidden-variable DAG functionals, while the general data-fusion efficiency papers assume source-alignment structures rather than an endogenous selector whose support and parameter-image equalities are part of the model. A fixed-H circuit is a rational function of one multinomial law, but its denominators, shared cells, and retained image constraints must be differentiated without pretending that selector contexts are independent samples. Boundary-uniform behavior is an additional obstacle and is not resolved by a pointwise interior calculation.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A symbolic derivative rule mapping every epsilon-interior rational identification circuit F(p_H) to its finite-table influence function, plus a plug-in or one-step estimator with a pointwise asymptotically normal limit and consistently estimable variance.

writing_exemplar.why: Its motivation turns the gap between graphical identification algorithms and usable estimators into the central problem.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: complete graphical algorithms output complicated functionals -> those functionals are underused because estimation is unclear -> fixing structure yields influence-function estimators -> selector-aware rational circuits need an analogous automatic inference layer

method_exemplars.technique: Differentiate fixing-based causal functionals, express the gradient as an observed-data influence function, and construct regular asymptotically linear estimators.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The target circuits are likewise compositions of finite probability kernels generated by graphical fixing operations.

method_exemplars.technique: Characterize influence functions and the efficient influence function under general multi-source alignment operators.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It supplies a general fused-data calculus against which the more constrained endogenous-selector tangent model can be compared.

literature_map:
Lee, Ghassami, and Shpitser (UAI 2024, arXiv:2404.06602) is the direct anchor: SS-ID is sound, most failed branches have witnesses, and completeness is explicitly conjectured.
Shpitser and Pearl (AAAI 2006) provide the ordinary ID template: recursive district reduction paired with hedge models witnessing every algorithmic failure.
Lee, Correa, and Bareinboim (UAI 2020) give gID completeness for arbitrary surrogate experiments through hedgelets and thickets.
Kivva, Mokhtarian, Etesami, and Kiyavash (UAI 2022, arXiv:2206.01081) show that the exact positivity regime can invalidate both soundness and an earlier completeness proof.
Bareinboim and Pearl (AAAI 2012) prove complete transportability in selection diagrams, where domains are supplied rather than generated by an endogenous random selector.
Bareinboim and Tian (AAAI 2015) characterize selection-bias recovery completely for Markovian models and give sufficient results in semi-Markovian models.
Tikka, Hyttinen, and Karvanen (NeurIPS 2019, arXiv:2009.09768) show that general context-specific identification is NP-hard and provide a sound search rather than general completeness.
Mokhtarian, Jamshidi, Etesami, and Kiyavash (AISTATS 2022, arXiv:2110.12064) prove completeness when context-specific control variables are observed roots, a strict special case of selector-gated CS-SCMs.
Chen and Darwiche (NeurIPS 2024, arXiv:2412.02869) compile logical and parameter constraints into arithmetic circuits but do not give fixed-support selector normalization or complete negative certificates.
Tabell, Tikka, and Karvanen (JMLR 2026, arXiv:2505.15215) add multi-source pruning and clustering with sufficient transfer conditions but no fixed-support selector converse.
Tikka and Karvanen (JMLR 2018, arXiv:1806.07085) provide the single-source pruning precursor and motivate preservation of identifying formulas.
Zhang, Tian, and Bareinboim (ICML 2022, arXiv:2110.05690) establish finite canonical SCM response types and polynomial-program bounds for heterogeneous inputs.
Tikka, Hyttinen, and Karvanen (JSS 2021, DOI:10.18637/jss.v099.i05) make arbitrary-source identification operational and use failed searches to suggest additional evidence, but not structurally legal selector-context additions.
Bhattacharya, Nabi, and Shpitser (JMLR 2022, arXiv:2003.12659), Li and Luedtke (Biometrika 2023), and Graham, Carone, and Rotnitzky (arXiv:2409.09973) supply nearby influence-function machinery but not inference for fixed-support CS-SCM circuits.
Targeted searches combining systematic selection with fixed support or selector support found no primary completion; the closest follow-up was Tabell et al.'s general pruning and clustering work.
prior_proposal_map:

The sole proposal-core-like artifact was the v1 POMDP attempt under stat_pomdp_latent_overlap_minimax.
Its seed_details[3] yielded one structurally transferable direction: simultaneous observationally equivalent hidden refinements.
Its honest_scope and technical_internal_limitation concerned latent-state cardinality and trajectory-likelihood factorization rather than systematic selection.
The available panel and partial-identification reviewer JSONs contained no strengthening_paths, published-prior-art calls, or relevant novelty flags.
No rejected-angle proposal, legacy proposal, bank README or writeup, or useful pipeline-summary artifact was present.
Accordingly, prior-proposal evidence augments only the global-twin lifting opportunity and does not independently support the normalization or pruning directions.
